issues.body: yaml.safe_load is not a semantics-preserving model of GitHub Actions workflow YAML. In particular, PyYAML's default YAML 1.1 resolver coerces keys such as `on` and `true` to the same boolean key. Thus changing a workflow's top-level `on:` key to `true:` can produce equal Python objects even though GitHub Actions interprets the files differently. Other lossy normalization and duplicate-key cases create the same general risk. Because membership in yaml_inert bypasses the `.github/` full-run trigger, this is a wrong-skip soundness bug, contradicting the stated fail-closed contract.
issues.fix_hint: Prove that the edit itself consists only of comments/whitespace outside scalar content, using a token- or diff-based method that preserves YAML spelling, tags, duplicate keys, and parser dialect semantics; do not infer GitHub Actions equivalence from PyYAML object equality. Add a regression test demonstrating that `on:` versus `true:` (and preferably duplicate-key/normalized-scalar collisions) is not inert. If retaining parsing, use a parser/configuration matching the consumer and reject any ambiguous or lossy construct before allowing the carve-out.
issues.title: PyYAML equality can falsely classify behavior-changing workflow edits as inert

verdict.summary: The proposed parsed-YAML equality check is not a sound proof of GitHub Actions behavioral equivalence. PyYAML safe_load applies YAML 1.1 coercions and discards representation details, while GitHub Actions uses different workflow parsing semantics. Consequently, a behavior-changing workflow edit can compare equal and be labeled YAML-INERT, incorrectly suppressing the full Rust matrix. The tests cover ordinary comments, block scalars, and a simple value change, but do not exercise parser-dialect or lossy-normalization collisions.
